newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba sees C$55.7 mln surplus in fiscal 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba sees C$55.7 mln surplus in fiscal 1996/97.

text.p: The Canadian province of Manitoba said on Friday it forecast a budget surplus in fiscal 1996/97 (Apr/Mar) of C$55.7 million.
The forecast surplus exceeds the prior projection of a C$21.8 million surplus by C$33.9 million, the government of Manitoba said in a statement.
"This is the second consecutive year a surplus will be achieved," said Manitoba Finance Minister Eric Stefanson.
The higher surplus stems from a projected C$118.4 million rise in revenues offset by a C$84.5 million rise in spending.
The changes are consistent with second quarter trends.
About C$81 million in the increased revenues come from more individual and corporate tax receipts, along with C$14 million more in retail sales tax and about C$25 million in other tax receipts.
Net proceeds from the sale of Manitoba Telecom Services was estimated at C$410 million and will be folded into the province's consolidated revenue fund.
Manitoba also said it would use C$150 million from the MTS sale revenues to pay down health sector debt.
The balance of the MTS divestiture, about C$260 million, will be transferred to Manitoba's fiscal stabilization fund.
